nodes.name: Hydrothermal NiVOH/NF synthesis
nodes.procedure: A solution comprising 0.3 g of nickel nitrate hexahydrate [Ni(NO₃)₂·6H₂O], 0.1 g of vanadium chloride (VCl₃), and 0.12 g of urea [CO(NH₂)₂] was added to 20 ml of deionized water (DI). The mixture underwent ultrasonication to ensure uniform dispersion of the solution. The mixture was then transferred to a Teflon reactor containing a pretreated 1.5×2.0 cm NF and reacted at 120°C for 12 hours. After cooling to room temperature, the sample was washed thoroughly several times with DI water and anhydrous ethanol, then dried in a vacuum oven and labeled as NiVOH/NF.

nodes.name: Ammonolysis to Ni₃N@V₂O₃/NF
nodes.procedure: The NiVOH/NF precursor was placed in a ceramic boat and treated with ammonia gas at a flow rate of 80 ml min⁻¹. The temperature was raised to 400°C at a rate of 5°C min⁻¹ and held for 2 hours to obtain a black product, denoted as Ni₃N@V₂O₃/NF.

nodes.name: Pt-Ni₃N@V₂O₃/NF impregnation
nodes.procedure: A 2-ml solution of chloroplatinic acid hexahydrate [H₂PtCl₆·6H₂O analytical reagent (AR) grade, Pt ≥ 37.5% with a concentration of 5 mg ml⁻¹] was diluted to 5 ml using DI water. The Ni₃N@V₂O₃/NF sample was then immersed in the solution and kept at room temperature for 1 hour to prepare the Pt-Ni₃N@V₂O₃/NF catalyst. The catalyst loading on the NF was about 1.4 mg cm⁻². Pt-Ni₃N/NF was prepared in the absence of VCl₃.

nodes.name: Hydrothermal NiFe LDH/NF synthesis
nodes.procedure: 0.2990 g of nickel nitrate hexahydrate [Ni(NO₃)₂·6H₂O], 0.1385 g of iron nitrate nonahydrate [Fe(NO₃)₃·9H₂O], and 0.1287 g of [CO(NH₂)₂] were dissolved in 15 ml of DI water using ultrasonication. The resulting solution was then transferred to Teflon reactor and the pretreated clean NF (2.0×3.0 cm) was immersed in it and placed in an oven at 120°C for 12 hours. After natural cooling, it was rinsed three times with DI water to remove loosely adhered particles.

nodes.name: Pt-C/NF electrode preparation
nodes.procedure: 5 mg of the catalyst was dispersed in a mixture solution containing 500 μl of isopropanol, 480 μl of DI water, and 20 μl of Nafion 117 solution (5.0 wt %). The mixture was then sonicated for 30 min to obtain a homogeneous suspension. Using a pipette, 70 μl of the catalyst ink was coated onto a clean NF surface (0.25 cm²) and then dried in a vacuum oven for 2 hours. The loading of commercial Pt-C is about 1.4 mg cm⁻².
nodes.source_text: Preparation of commercial Pt-C/NF reference electrode... about 1.4 mg cm⁻².

The HER performances of Pt-Ni3N@V2O3/NF... in 1 M KOH are tested using a standard three-electrode system at room temperature (figs. S15 to S25). The linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) curve obtained at a scan rate of 2 mV s⁻¹ reveals that Pt-Ni3N@V2O3/NF exhibits the lowest overpotential, requiring only 15 mV to achieve a current density of 10 mA cm⁻²... required only an overpotential of 68.4 mV to achieve... 500 mA cm⁻²... Tafel slope... 20.5 mV dec⁻¹... double-layer capacitance... 157.1 mF cm⁻²... Hupd peak... 0.187 V... operated without degradation at... 100 and 500 mA cm⁻² for at least 240 hours

nodes.description: HER performance in 1 M KOH + seawater
nodes.source_text: Pt-Ni3N@V2O3/NF maintains the highest catalytic activity even in seawater, requiring only 21, 47, and 80 mV of overpotential to achieve current densities of 10, 100, and 500 mA cm⁻²... mass activity... 9.751 A mgPt⁻¹, which is 30.86 times higher than that of Pt-C/NF (0.316 A mgPt⁻¹)... Tafel slope value of 23.4 mV dec⁻¹... operate continuously for 500 hours at current density of 500 mA cm⁻²... high hydrogen production rate (2.0 ml min⁻¹ cm⁻²) in seawater and the near-perfect Faraday efficiency

nodes.description: AEMWE performance in 1 M KOH + seawater at room temperature
nodes.source_text: Pt-Ni3N@V2O3/NF-based AEMWE exhibits higher electrolytic seawater activity compared to electrolyzers based on Pt-Ni3N/NF and Pt-C/NF. Specifically, in 1 M KOH + seawater electrolyte at room temperature, only 1.89 V is required to drive 0.5 A cm⁻²... exhibit excellent durability, maintaining stable operation for at least 100 hours

nodes.characterization_summary: Powder XRD patterns confirm the presence of a composite phase comprising Ni₃N, V₂O₃, and Pt in Pt-Ni₃N@V₂O₃/NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The powder x-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns, as illustrated in Fig. 1A and fig. S3, confirm the presence of a composite phase comprising Ni₃N, V₂O₃, and Pt.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows Pt-Ni₃N@V₂O₃/NF exhibits granular morphology with rough surface; Ni₃N@V₂O₃/NF exhibits interconnected porous structures.
nodes.evidence_snippet: After ammonolysis, scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) show that Ni₃N@V₂O₃/NF exhibit interconnected porous structures (fig. S6)... After the incorporation of Pt, SEM and TEM analyses reveal that Pt-Ni₃N@V₂O₃/NF exhibits a granular morphology, together with a rough surface (Fig. 1, B and C).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM reveals Pt nanoparticles with average size of 4.41 nm formed in situ on Pt-Ni₃N@V₂O₃/NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Pt nanoparticles, formed in situ, have an average particle size of 4.41 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows amorphous/low crystallinity V₂O₃ covers the outer surface of Pt-Ni₃N@V₂O₃/NF with lattice stripes of 0.203 nm and 0.226 nm corresponding to (111) facets of Ni₃N and Pt.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) shows that amorphous/low crystallinity V₂O₃ covers the outer surface of Pt-Ni₃N@V₂O₃/NF (Fig. 1D), with lattice stripes of 0.203 and 0.226 nm corresponding to the (111) facets of Ni₃N and the (111) facets of Pt (Fig. 1, E to G), respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM images, EDS elemental mapping, and EDS line scan show internal larger nanoparticles comprise Ni₃N, V₂O₃ distributed in surrounding region, and uniformly anchored small-sized Pt nanoparticles on surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Fig. 1 (H and I), high-angle annular dark-field scanning TEM (HAADF-STEM) images, energy-dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) elemental mapping, and EDS line scan collectively suggest that the internal larger nanoparticles comprise Ni₃N, while V₂O₃ is distributed in the surrounding region.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS determines Pt content of approximately 6.61% in Pt-Ni₃N@V₂O₃/NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The content of Pt is determined by energy dispersive x-ray spectroscopy to be approximately 6.61%

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES analysis confirms Pt content of 6.94% in Pt-Ni₃N@V₂O₃/NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: which is consistent with the results of inductively coupled plasma-optical emission spectrometry (ICP-OES) analysis (6.94%).

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution XPS Ni 2p shows peak at ~853 eV corresponding to partially positively charged Ni in Ni₃N@V₂O₃/NF, Pt-Ni₃N/NF and Pt-Ni₃N@V₂O₃/NF with clear shift toward higher binding energy for Ni(II) and Ni(+) in Pt-Ni₃N@V₂O₃/NF; V 2p shows Pt-Ni₃N@V₂O₃/NF (21.7% V(III)) vs Ni₃N@V₂O₃/NF (64.9% V(III)); characteristic peaks of Pt metal and N 1s show positive shift.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the high-resolution Ni 2p x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) spectra (Fig. 2A), the peak at approximately 853 eV corresponds to partially positively charged Ni in Ni₃N@V₂O₃/NF, Pt-Ni₃N/NF and Pt-Ni₃N@V₂O₃/NF... We observe a clear shift toward higher binding energy for both Ni(II) and Ni(+) in Pt-Ni₃N@V₂O₃/NF compared to Ni₃N@V₂O₃/NF... high-resolution XPS spectra of V 2p demonstrate that the Pt-Ni₃N@V₂O₃/NF catalyst (21.7%) exhibits a markedly lower content of V(III) compared to the Ni₃N@V₂O₃/NF catalyst (64.9%) (Fig. 2B).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge XANES of Ni₃N@V₂O₃/NF and Pt-Ni₃N@V₂O₃/NF resemble Ni foil (metallic Ni); Pt L3-edge confirms metallic Pt phase in Pt-Ni₃N@V₂O₃/NF; V K-edge matches V₂O₃.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ni K-edge x-ray absorption near edge structure (XANES) spectra of Ni₃N@V₂O₃/NF and Pt-Ni₃N@V₂O₃/NF closely resemble those of Ni foil (Fig. 2D), suggesting that the Ni exists mainly in the metallic phase... The K-edge of V for Ni₃N@V₂O₃/NF and Pt-Ni₃N@V₂O₃/NF in Fig. 2E is nearly identical to that of V₂O₃... The presence of Pt in Pt-Ni₃N@V₂O₃/NF as a predominantly metallic phase is confirmed by the proximity of the Pt L3-edge in Pt-Ni₃N@V₂O₃/NF to that of the Pt foil.

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-EXAFS shows Ni-N bond length increases and Ni-Ni decreases in Pt-Ni₃N@V₂O₃/NF; Pt-Pt bond length 2.748 Å and Pt-O 2.003 Å indicating metallic Pt predominates.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Notably, with the addition of Pt, the Ni-N bond length in Pt-Ni₃N@V₂O₃/NF increases while the Ni-Ni bond length decreases... The fitting results indicate that the Pt-Pt bond length in Pt-Ni₃N@V₂O₃/NF is 2.748 Å with slight oxidation of the Pt-O bond (2.003 Å).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge FT-EXAFS shows Ni-N bond length increase and Ni-Ni bond length decrease in Pt-Ni₃N@V₂O₃/NF vs Ni₃N@V₂O₃/NF; Pt L3-edge fitting gives Pt-Pt bond length 2.748 Å and Pt-O 2.003 Å.
nodes.evidence_snippet: After the introduction of Pt, the Ni K-edge in Pt-Ni₃N@V₂O₃/NF shifted toward a higher binding energy compared to Ni₃N@V₂O₃/NF... with the addition of Pt, the Ni-N bond length in Pt-Ni₃N@V₂O₃/NF increases while the Ni-Ni bond length decreases... The fitting results indicate that the Pt-Pt bond length in Pt-Ni₃N@V₂O₃/NF is 2.748Å with slight oxidation of the Pt-O bond (2.003 Å).
